However efficient optimization of absorbers for a range of angles of incidence still poses challenges. In this work, we explore how selection of the GA objective function can increase the absorber bandwidth without increasing the thickness for a range of angles of incidence.

articleTitle: Analysis of the internal scattering field distribution in an oversized rectangular slotted waveguide
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: A rectangular parallel-plate slot array fed by a post-wall waveguide is an attractive candidate for high-efficiency and mass-producible planar antennas in millimeterwave applications. The transmission loss is small in the waveguide in comparison with microstrip-type feed lines and the fabrication cost of simple via-holing and etching is low. The design is conducted assuming plane wave propagation, neglecting both the boundary conditions at the narrow walls and the slot coupling perturbation; this is effective only for an extremely large aperture and weakly coupled slots. Since the EM analysis for the actual structure seems too heavy, the key for the advanced design of the parallel plate waveguide arrays is to establish accurate, but still simple models, for the analysis and design. This paper discusses the fast evaluation of slot scattering inside the parallel plate waveguide. It gives the basis for future approximate but accurate analysis/design methods for parallel plate slotted waveguide arrays.

articleTitle: FDTD formulation for bianisotropic medium
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: The FDTD method firstly proposed by K.S. Yee (see IEEE Trans., vol.AP-14, p.302-7, 1966) has been successfully applied to the numerical analysis of various electromagnetic problems, including scattering, antennas, microwave circuits and EM compatibility. Recently, FDTD formulations for some complex media, such as dispersive or anisotropic medium (see Luebbers, R.J. et al, IEEE Trans., vol.EMC-32, p.222-7, 1990; Schneider, J., et al, IEEE Trans., vol.AP-41, p.994-9, 1993) have been studied. However, the formulation of FDTD for bianisotropic medium has not been reported yet, due to the difficulty of treating the coupling between electric/magnetic constituents. In order to establish the FDTD formulae, both the iterative approximation in space difference and time difference are successfully employed. Furthermore, these formulae may be degenerated into the cases of anisotropic, isotropic or biisotropic media.

articleTitle: Detection and imaging of buried homogeneous dielectric objects
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: With reference to the detection of buried homogeneous dielectric objects (such as landmines or cavities), a simple regularization scheme is proposed which achieves a good rejection of spurious inclusions as well as false targets. The proposed approach also allows roughness to be managed as a retrievable unknown.

articleTitle: FDTD calculation of SAR for the monopole antenna on the conducting box with the metallic folder
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: This paper presents the numerically simulated specific absorption rate (SAR) within the human head due to a folding cellular telephone. The frequency considered was 825 MHz and the time averaged radiated power of 0.6 W was used. The influence on SAR of the geometrical change of folder length and the connection position between folder and body has been analyzed for the homogeneous head model.

articleTitle: A robust test apparatus for electromagnetic compatibility testing and improvement utilizing a network analyzer
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: A simple but rigorous test apparatus is presented and validated experimentally, which provides not only an accurate and effective electromagnetic (EM) immunity testing system, but also accurately characterizes the EM immunity spectrum of an equipment under test. The apparatus utilizes the features of a network analyzer (NA) along with directional couplers and a power meter. It also provides accurate EM interference environment measurement without a field strength meter. This proposed test apparatus provides not only an accurate and effective EM immunity testing system, but also accurately characterizes the EM immunity spectrum of a device under test. An immunity test for a digital transmission system was conducted to verify the effectiveness of this test apparatus. The failure frequencies of this equipment under test (EUT) are detected within the measured immunity spectrum.

articleTitle: Fast full-wave moment method for the analysis of finite aperture-coupled microstrip patch arrays
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: An efficient spectral domain moment method is presented to analyze the radiation from large finite aperture-coupled microstrip patch arrays. Based on the combination of the equivalence principle and the reciprocity method, the resulting system of integral equations is discretized using subdomain expansion functions in a Galerkin approach. The integrals are represented in the spectral domain and evaluated using special techniques. For typical array dimensions this leads to a large system of linear equations which is solved by the BCG-FFT method. Due to the incorporated simultaneous electric and magnetic surface current densities the BCG algorithm shows usually a slow convergence behaviour, a technique is derived which avoids compound surface current densities of different types in the iterative process. Results for arrays up to 256 elements demonstrate the flexibility of the method, comparisons with available measurements verify its accuracy.

articleTitle: Implementation of formulations for dielectric material and perfect conductors in G2DMULT
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: G2DMULT is a general algorithm for the calculation of spectral Green's functions of two-dimensional (2D) multiregion structures by using the method of moments (MoM) (see Kildal, P.-S., Proc. 1999 IEEE APS Symp., p.2200-03, 1999). When we have these spectral Green's functions, we can efficiently find the radiation characteristics of three-dimensional (3D) antennas in the vicinity of the 2D structures. The algorithm makes use of the Fourier transformation of the 3D sources in the uniform direction of the structure to arrive into a spectral domain problem that can be solved by a 2D spatial technique. G2DMULT solves for the unknown tangential fields on the boundaries of the material regions. This paper describes an implementation of the formulations for both dielectric materials and perfect conductors in G2DMULT. The code is applied to and verified against existing results for scattering from dielectric loaded so-called hard cylinders and calculation of the radiation pattern of a base station antenna.

articleTitle: Iterative spectrum analysis for pre-cleaning of narrow-band interference from radar data
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: Examples of pre-cleaning of ionograms are presented by using a new method of spectrum analysis of 512 complex data samples, independently in the period after each transmitter pulse. The exact amplitude and exact frequency of the four largest interference signals are determined in the partial spectrum and subtracted from the time-domain data. A new spectrum is created from the modified data of a single pulse period until the remaining spectral amplitude peaks are less than 10 dB above the running average spectral amplitude. After this procedure the total data are processed the standard way. In contrast to all known methods of filtering the time-domain data (to reduce the leakage caused by the finite data sampling length) and the "punching out" of spectral lines with large amplitude, this method has the least effect on the amplitude and phase of the wanted data.

articleTitle: Fast multipole method and microlocal discretization for the 3-D Helmholtz equation
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: A numerical solution of the boundary integral equation for the exterior Helmholtz problem in three dimensions, leads to the solution of a dense linear system. In order to have a well conditioned system, we consider the Despres integral equations (see J. Electromag. Waves and Appl., vol.13, p.1553-68, 1999). An iterative method is given by Despres to solve this system. If Niter is the number of the iterations, the complexity of this resolution is of order Niter k/sup 4/, where k is the wave number. In order to speed up the iterative solution of the system, we have considered the coupling of two methods, the microlocal discretization method and the fast multipole method (FMM). The microlocal discretization method of T. Abboud, J.-C. Nedelec and B. Zhou (1995), enables one to consider a new system whose size is of order k/sup 2/3//spl times/k/sup 2/3/ instead of k/sup 2//spl times/k/sup 2/ for convex geometries. However, due to the geometrical approximation of the surface, the fine mesh of the standard case is still considered. Another method, the fast multipole method, is one of the most efficient and robust methods used to speed up the calculation of matrix-vector products, with a cost of order k/sup 3/ instead of k/sup 4/ for the one level FMM. In this paper, a coupling of these two methods is presented. It enables one to reduce the CPU time very efficiently for large wave number, with a complexity of order k/sup 3/+Niter k/sup 4/3/.

articleTitle: A helical antenna with a self-complementary shape
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: The authors propose a bifilar helical antenna with a self-complementary shape. Bifilar helical antennas having an omnidirectional radiation pattern often have been composed of thin wires . In these conventional shapes, it is difficult to design an antenna satisfying both desired characteristics of the radiation and the reflection because the design parameters, such as antenna diameter, simultaneously influence these characteristics. The proposed antenna has an input impedance of which the conductance is almost constant by applying a self-complementary shape to the antenna structure. This technique allows selection of the optimal antenna diameter for the radiation characteristic independent of its impedance matching.

articleTitle: A semi-analytical formulation for investigating the radiation characteristics of traveling wave slot antennas
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: A semi-analytical formulation for the analysis of the far field of a CWSA (constant width slot antenna) using the reciprocity theorem is presented. The method provides a good physical insight into the operation of the traveling wave slot antenna and at the same time introduces an approach that can easily be extended to the analysis of other types of tapered slot antenna.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic measurement system requirements
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: This paper focuses on the requirements for antenna and/or RCS measurement systems. It is shown that traditional methods are not satisfactory because they do not take into account the impact of errors on critical measurements to be performed in the range. In order for a facility to perform well, the range stray signals are required to be smaller in magnitude for wider angles relative to the desired plane wave. Thus, one must deal with each potential error source one-at-a-time through simulation to insure that it meets or is better than the required error magnitude for that angle of incidence. The error level requirement as a function of angle is based on the most challenging measurements to be performed in the new range. The completed facility should then be evaluated to insure that it achieves the desired performance level. If error terms are spotted, they should be corrected using the numerous techniques found in the literature. If the error term cannot be corrected, the range operator should make note of that error and attempt to ascertain its impact on any future measurements performed in the facility. This will lead to greatly improved ranges which ultimately produce superior measurements.

articleTitle: Spectral Green's functions for multilayered bianisotropic media
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: We derive the spectral Green's function of a multilayered structure involving bianisotropic materials. Such materials offer new degrees of freedom to improve, besides, the radiation properties of multilayered structures. We propose an analytical study in the spectral domain of bianisotropic layers that are characterized in terms of transmission matrices leading to an equivalent circuit representation of the whole multilayered structure. Finally, a numerical result is presented for the special case of the chirostrip antenna consisting of a single chiral grounded slab.

articleTitle: Analysis of a conformal cavity-backed patch antenna using a hybrid MoM/FEM technique
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: In this paper we present an analysis of a conformal, cavity-backed, co-ax fed microstrip patch antenna, using a combination of the method of moments (MoM) and the finite element method (FEM). A domain decomposition approach is employed to partition the problem into two, each of which is analyzed by using the technique that is best suited for the individual domain. Specifically, the cavity region, which contains a combination of inhomogeneous dielectrics and PEC objects, is treated with the FEM, whereas the MoM is applied to the outer surface, which is assumed to be a perfect conductor.

articleTitle: An apply of hybrid GA for array pattern control of quasi-zenithal satellite's Earth station antenna
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: The quasi-zenithal satellite (figure-8 satellite) system is a satellite constellation consisting of three or more satellites placed in inclined geosynchronous circular orbits with an identical inclination of around 45 degrees. At any time, at least one of the three satellites is moving near the zenith view from, for example, Japan. The sub-satellite point traces a so called "figure of eight" locus on the ground, elongating in the north-south direction with an arbitrary point on the equator in the center. Dual use of the same frequency can be applied between geostationary satellites and quasi-zenithal satellites in the fixed-satellite service (FSS). The beam antenna at the earth station used in the FSS can separate spatially the signal of the quasi-zenithal satellite from that of geostationary satellites by using its radiation pattern.. A radiation pattern control method for the phased array antenna of the fixed station of a quasi-zenithal satellite is described. We introduce a hybrid genetic algorithm (GA) technique, which is a combination of GA and the descend method.

articleTitle: Narrow-waisted Gaussian beam discretization for pulsed radiation from 2D large apertures
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: In this paper, we present a computationally efficient and physically appealing discretized Gabor-based parameterization, in terms of narrow-waisted ray-like pulsed Gaussian beams, for the three-dimensional (3D) vector electromagnetic fields radiated from short-pulsed arbitrarily polarized large 2D truncated aperture distributions. This analysis extends the time-harmonic results in Maciel and Felsen (2000) to the time domain (TD), following the guidelines of our previous investigation of pulsed radiation of 2D fields from 1D large truncated apertures (Galdi et al. 2000).

articleTitle: Efficient non-uniform orthogonal mesh generation algorithm for cylindrical FDTD applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: The paper presents an efficient non-uniform, orthogonal mesh generation algorithm for the analysis and design of cylindrical microwave devices and integrated circuits using the cylindrical finite-difference time-domain (CFDTD) methods. By using this algorithm, we can easily generate a suitable CFDTD grid which is fitting for the developed CFDTD Maxwell's solver.

articleTitle: Investigation of direct and inverse scattering problems for inhomogeneous medium
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: This paper considers the direct and inverse scattering problems for the refractive index in the case of a planar wave. Liouville's transform is employed for transforming the Helmholtz equation in the form of the Sturm equation with a simple relationship between potential in the Sturm equation and refractive index in the Helmholtz equation. The exact and approximate solutions of the inverse and direct problems are formulated. We considered the simplest case of a plane wave incident along the normal to the 1D profile of the refractive index (without dispersion and absorption). The exact and approximate solutions are obtained for two representations of the field in an inhomogeneous layer: (i) in the form of two waves propagating locally in forward and back directions; (ii) using lost functions (the second representation results in the appearance of the well known Gel'fand-Levitan integral equation). It is shown that the first approximations corresponding to single backscattering are similar for both the representations. These results can be easily generalized for the case of an arbitrary angle of incidence of a plane wave.

articleTitle: Biological effect of mobile telephone inside the human brain
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: This paper presents the results from an extensive numerical simulation of the effect of the mobile telephone inside the human brain The aim of this paper is to build a simulation model of real mobile telephone and combine it with the simulation model of the human brain. The combined method of moments (MoM) and generalized multipole technique (GMT) is used to determine and study the electromagnetic field (EF) and the absorbed power (AP) induced inside various models of biological body or human brain. The computed results with this combination technique demonstrate the accuracy of each implementation. The computed (EF) has a special or important meaning for the distributed (EF) induced inside the human brain. For the particular geometry simulated. the presence of the head model is taken with different views.

articleTitle: A new measurement method for four-port scattering matrix of a dual-polarization antenna
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: A new method to measure the four-port scattering matrix of a dual-polarization antenna is proposed. A two-port vector network analyzer is connected to the two excitation ports of the antenna to measure its 2/spl times/2 scattering matrix. The formulation is developed to solve the four-port scattering matrix of the dual polarization antenna from the measured two-port scattering matrix with two calibration scattering objects.

articleTitle: Aperture-coupled coplanar patch antennas
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: Aperture-coupled coplanar patch antennas (CPA) were investigated. The antennas were simulated with a commercial simulator, and then four samples were fabricated and measured. The comparison between the aperture-coupled CPA and the aperture-coupled microstrip patch antenna (MPA) with the same patch dimension was presented. The result shows that the return loss and the radiation pattern of the CPA are similar to the MPA, and the front-to-back ratio and the gain of the CPA are better than the MPA.

articleTitle: Time-domain imaging of radar targets using high frequency approximation methods
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: We investigate time domain imaging of aircraft employing sine-modulated exponential pulse (SMEP) responses, and interpret the reconstructed image from a new approach, based on analysis of the scattering mechanisms and the back-projection algorithm utilized in image retrieval. The time-domain inverse scattering identity with the incorporation of edge diffraction is derived and images of an aircraft model B-52 are shown.

articleTitle: Optical control on HEMT devices
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: Theoretical work for the DC characteristics of depletion mode Al/sub 0.3/Ga/sub 0.7/As/GaAs HEMTs under optical illumination is presented. Both the photoconductive effect, which increases the 2-DEG channel electron concentration, and the photovoltaic effect in the gate junction are discussed. Analysis of the effect of optical control on the gain of a HEMT amplifier and the optical tuning of a HEMT oscillator are further described.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic field coupling between cellular phones using FDTD analysis
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: The assessment of potential hazards caused by electromagnetic interference to electronic systems as well as transmission devices is an essential engineering task. The effect of nearby electrically active objects on the effective radiation characteristics of the phone is yet to be investigated. Examples of this situation include the presence of a similar radiating object nearby the cellular phone, the presence of reflecting objects, resonance conditions between different structures and frequency shift effects. In this paper, a detailed characterization of the effects of EM coupling on the performance of cellular phones placed in close proximity to each other is presented. The analysis is performed numerically using the FDTD method and is focused on the modification of the input impedance and radiation properties of the phone.

articleTitle: Characteristics of a helical array antenna radiating circularly polarized conical beam
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: This paper presents the characteristics of a helical array antenna radiating circularly polarized conical beam. The structure of the antenna is simple and easy to fabricate. The radiation pattern of the antenna is calculated by combining the total fields radiated from each small helical antenna on the ground plane. The effect of the finite size ground plane is taken into account and compared with one considered in case of the ground plane is infinite extent. The radiation patterns for various parameters viz., the array radius and the number of elements are demonstrated. Guidelines for the antenna design to realize the desired directivity and elevation angle are illustrated. The experiment is under investigation.

articleTitle: Diffraction by a curved impedance wedge of arbitrary angle
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: The methods generally considered for the diffraction by a wedge with curved faces are often different for a wedge of narrow or large angle. An original approach, initiated by J.M.L. Bernard (see Rev. Tech. Th., vol.23, no.2, p.321-30, 1991) for faces of constant curvatures and whose results have been recently used by V.A. Borovikov (see J. Comm. Techn. Elect., vol.43, no.12, p.1337-46, 1998) for his developments on the non constant curvature case, permits a new global asymptotic study for an impedance curved wedge of any angle. We reduce the boundary problem on the field to an asymptotic one on the spectral function, related to the representation of the field in the form of a Sommerfeld-Maliuzhinets integral. The functional equations then obtained can he solved, and the asymptotics of the spectral function are developed (see Bernard, 1991). We present a new form of it. An expression allowing the transition to an asymptotic expansion with fractional powers is also given for directions close to the tangent at the faces, where creeping waves excited by the edge propagate. We note that the general expressions here given allow the recovery of all known results on diffraction coefficients for particular wedge angles, from the case of a discontinuity of curvature to the case of a curved half plane.

articleTitle: A novel perfectly matched layer method for an unconditionally stable ADI-FDTD method
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: Recently an unconditionally stable ADI method was successfully applied to the solution of Maxwell's equations using a variation of the FDTD method. The ADI method is most useful for solving problems where the lattice is grossly over discretized spatially (< 10/sup -2//spl lambda//sub min/). For this scheme to be applicable to analyzing practical electromagnetic interaction problems, an efficient absorbing boundary condition that maintains unconditional stability must be derived. In this paper, an absorbing boundary condition using a perfectly matched layer (PML) is introduced. Specifically, the convolutional PML (CPML) method is used with complex frequency shifted scaling coefficients. It is shown that this method maintains unconditional stability. Further, it is demonstrated that the method provides a significant improvement in the reflection error as compared to the originally proposed split-field PML ADI scheme.

articleTitle: Application of FDTD method to conformal patch antennas
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: In this paper, we present an application of the conformal finite difference time domain (CFDTD) method to model a conformal patch antenna mounted on a coated PEC cylinder. We use the conformal technique and non-uniform mesh to model the entire antenna configuration including the PEC cylinder, the thin dielectric layer and the patch antenna as opposed to a hybrid approach that is sometimes utilized to solve this type of problem.

articleTitle: A local-ether wave equation and the Galilean-invariant electromagnetic force law
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: In a Galilean theory recently developed, the Lorentz force law has been modified in such a way that the electromagnetic force is invariant when observed in different inertial frames, as expected intuitively. In this investigation, based on the local-ether model of wave propagation, a Galilean-invariant wave equation is proposed. This wave equation incorporates a natural frequency and the electric scalar potential. A unique feature is that this potential connects to the augmentation operator which in turn is associated with the momentum operator and the velocity of the source particle. From this local-ether wave equation, a first-order time evolution equation is derived, which presents Galilean modifications of Schrodinger's equation. This modified equation in turn leads to the Galilean-invariant electromagnetic force law given in terms of the augmented potentials.

articleTitle: An implicit LU/AF FDTD method
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: This paper has introduced an implicit LU/AF FDTD method for computational electromagnetics. A second-order accurate LU/AF characteristic based algorithm for electromagnetics has been implemented and tested on one-dimensional model problems for uniform and nonuniform grids. The one-dimensional model problem results show that accurate solutions for wave propagation can be obtained using Courant number greater than one and the method works well with lossy dielectric materials. The results demonstrate potential advantages in a one dimensional context, and this approach appears promising for development of stable, accurate and efficient implicit LU/AF schemes for complex two and three dimensional applications. Extensions to two and three dimensional applications have been outlined.

articleTitle: Artifical neural network based buried land mine imaging
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: Our buried land mine imaging system is based on transmitting and receiving antennas mounted within a cylindrical auger, a stepped frequency CW transmitter/receiver, and three artificial neural network (ANN) imaging processors, all controlled by a small computer. Stepped frequency, CW microwave signals reflected from objects within the view of the transmitter and receive antennas are used as inputs to the first ANN processor. This paper briefly describes the design of broad RF bandwidth cylindrical waveguide antennas that are mounted in the opposite spades of a dual spaded auger, the training patterns used for ANN land mine imaging and experimental land mine images using data recorded in April 1999 at the USA army's A.P.Hill test site.

articleTitle: Estimation of inhomogeneous permittivity profiles of spherical objects from noisy scattering measurement data
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: An accurate method for reconstructing inhomogeneous permittivity profiles of spherically shaped objects from the measurement of noisy scattering data is presented. The overall reconstruction is achieved in two basic steps. In the first step, the direct problem is formulated to obtain a nonlinear differential equation involving a frequency dependent reflection coefficient in a spherical coordinate system. The second step involves the inversion of this nonlinear differential equation using our previously proposed renormalization technique to obtain the unknown permittivity profile of spherically shaped objects in terms of a spherical Fourier-Bessel transform of the measured reflection coefficient data. Several higher order TE- and TM-mode illuminations with different noise levels have been considered. A good agreement between the actual and the reconstructed profiles even under high noise conditions shows the validity of our proposed scheme.

articleTitle: On the accuracy of the complex image method
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: The far-field asymptotic expressions for the vector potential Green's function of an infinitesimal vertical magnetic dipole (VMD), radiating above a half-space, are used to explain the failure of the standard CI method, when the source and observer are near to the interface, but separated by a large lateral distance. In these types of problems the field at the observation point is dominated by a lateral wave that is not modeled accurately by the standard Cl method. It is shown for the first time that by applying the Cl approximation process over a different path in the k/sub z0/ plane, the accuracy and robustness of the Cl method for such a problem geometry can be improved.

articleTitle: A CMOS IC for RF programmable surface acoustic wave filter
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: A 1 /spl mu/m CMOS integrated circuit has been designed and fabricated for an RF programmable surface acoustic wave filter. It has sampling, weighting, controlling and summing functions. There are eight identical cells in the chip. Each cell has a parallel sampling input which can get the RF signal from each tap of the delay line type (TDL) SAW filter or from each terminal in a set of the IDT filter. Two double aluminum layers and one poly-silicon layer sandwich capacitors C1 and C2 are used as the coupling capacitors in series for sampling. A low on-resistance NMOS transistor T1 with high W/L value (500) is used for weighting and summing. Its on-resistance can be changed in a large dynamic range with the variation of an analog weighting voltage (0-5 volt) in its gate. The output signal voltage will be changed by varying its on-resistance to realize the weighting function. All the drains of the T1 transistors in each cell are connected to realize the summing function. The input of the weighting analog voltage is controlled by another NMOS transistor (W/L=100) T2 and an 8 bit shift register. This IC has been fabricated and tested. The chip size is 3 mm /spl times/ 1 mm. A 16.6 dB on/off ratio and a 13.6 dB insertion loss in each bit of the IC is obtained in testing. This IC is connected with a set of multi-IDT SAW devices to realize a programmable SAW filter. A 13.0 dB on/off ratio and 17.3 dB insertion loss in each bit is obtained also in programmable SAW filter circuit. This CMOS IC chip is also used with a LiNbO/sub 3/ SAW chip to form a programmable SAW filter using MCM packaging.

articleTitle: Galerkin-MoM analysis for dielectric scatters by using sinusoidal reaction technique
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: The Galerkin-MoM analysis was reported, where the uniform function is used as the basis and test functions, and the double volume integral was reduced to a triple integral. However, the discontinuity of the polarization current between the neighboring dielectric blocks still remains because of use of the uniform basis function. In this paper, a method using the sinusoidal functions for the basis and test functions is presented to avoid the problem of the discontinuity. The mutual impedance between the dielectric blocks is expressed as a triple integral form instead of the double volume integral. Numerical results are shown to demonstrate the accuracy and the short CPU time of the proposed procedure.

articleTitle: Numerical integrations in higher order loop-star method of moments for computational electromagnetics
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: In using the Galerkin-type loop-star method of moment to solve electromagnetic problems, it is necessary to compute double integrals. The objective in this report is to determine the appropriate numerical integration rule.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave antennas fed by high permittivity LSE-NRD guide
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: The tapered high permittivity LSE-NRD guide has been investigated as a radiator. It has interesting properties such as a broad radiation pattern and simple structure. A fan beam antenna at 35 GHz and the planar antenna at 60 GHz have been developed successfully for several kinds of millimeter-wave applications. We are thinking positively of applying the high permittivity LSE-NRD guide in the fields of millimeter wave antennas.

articleTitle: CAD of multilayer conformal cylindrical arrays
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: The new trends in the communication market are demanding wider bandwidths and consequently higher frequencies and higher bit rates. The traditional hardware development, based on the manufacture and measurement of test components, is too expensive and time consuming. The availability of novel integrated design tools and manufacturing techniques is therefore an essential requirement. In this paper, we present an accurate and efficient tool for the analysis of multilayer conformal cylindrical arrays of open-ended waveguides, based on a multimode equivalent network (MEN) formulation.

articleTitle: Phase conjugation array using subharmonically injection locked self-oscillating mixers
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: A novel approach is developed and tested for achieving phase conjugation. Using anti-symmetric pair of subharmonically injection locked selfoscillating mixers (SILSOM), which oscillate at /spl omega/, an input signal at /spl omega//2 will be converted to its conjugated signal. No external RF source is needed for LO pumping, and the input and output signals will be the same frequency due to the locking phenomenon of the oscillators. The proposed phase conjugation array finds its application in a retro-directive antenna array.

articleTitle: Development of an integrated multi-grid 3D FDTD and finite-difference heat transfer code to simulate microwave drying in multimode cavities
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: In this paper, we describe the development of a unified code for simulating microwave processing of materials in multimode cavities. The integrated codes include a multi-grid 3D FDTD code and a finite difference heat transfer program. The code was used to simulate various feed options for the microwave cavity to help control and improve the uniformity of heating. The heat transfer code together with knowledge of the dielectric properties of materials as a function of temperature, which is also measured in our laboratory, provide significant information that help design controlled and high-yield microwave drying processes. Simulation results from both the multi-grid FDTD and the heat transfer codes are described, and suggestions for optimizing the drying uniformity discussed.

articleTitle: Modifications of the Lorentz force law invariant under Galilean transformations
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: It is generally expected from intuition that the electromagnetic force exerted on a charged particle should be invariant as observed in different inertial frames. In the special relativity, this invariance is achieved by invoking the Lorentz transformation of space and time. In this investigation, an entirely different interpretation of this force invariance is presented by proposing a Galilean-invariant model of the electromagnetic force. In this new classical model, the electromagnetic force is expressed in terms of the augmented scalar potential. This new potential is a modification of the electric scalar potential by incorporating an ordinarily small velocity-dependent part. Each of the position vectors, time derivatives, and velocities involved in the proposed force law is referred specifically to a respective reference frame. By virtue of this feature, the electromagnetic force is endowed with the unique property of Galilean invariance. The velocity-dependent parts of the proposed force look quite different from their counterparts in the Lorentz force. However, under the common low-speed condition where the source particles forming the current drift very slowly in a matrix, the proposed Galilean-invariant model reduces to the Lorentz force law, if the latter is observed in the matrix frame as done in common practice.

articleTitle: A study of transfer function estimation error and a practical multibeam antenna system with precoding interference cancellation
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: Beyond IMT-2000, systems must use high ability interference canceling technology to achieve high speed and high capacity transmission. This paper proposes a kind of precoding technology that, in a practical manner, can completely cancel downlink interference in the same space and the same frequency band. The concept of this technology is to multiply the transmitting signal by the inverse matrix of the space transfer functions matrix sent by each mobile station. Its high interference cancellation performance is evaluated by considering the error in estimating the transfer function. A new scheme is proposed that is extremely practical because it eliminates the need to measure the delay. A fully implemented system is described.

articleTitle: RCS calculation for large inhomogeneous penetrable objects using a spectral integral equation solver
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: We attempt to solve large scale scattering problems of inhomogeneous bodies by solving a volume integral equation. We develop a spectral method using the FFT in the weak-form discretization of the integral equation. This spectral method requires O(Nlog/sub 2/N) CPU time and O(N) computer memory, where N is the number of unknowns. It converges several times faster than previous methods. With this spectral method, we are able to solve a large problem with over 12.7 million unknowns. We have validated our numerical results by comparing with Mie series for a multilayer spherical medium. The method has been used to model a large penetrable missile-like object.

articleTitle: Non-linear phenomena in catastrophe focusings
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: The main purpose of the present work is to research the influence of the weak non-linearity of the refraction index in the electromagnetic wave propagation in the vicinity of the catastrophe type focusing. The problem with a specially constructed phase screen, which creates in uniform media with linear refraction index focusing of the type under consideration, is investigated as a particular case for research. A flat electromagnetic wave falls on the phase screen and generates the focusing region behind the screen. The diffraction structure without any non-linearity is well known. It can be estimated, for example, by means Maslov's method of the canonical operator.

articleTitle: Estimation of the waveform of voltage exciting a monopole antenna to confirm magnetic field measurement
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: Electromagnetic fields radiated by electrostatic discharges (ESD) are major sources of electromagnetic interference. Such fast transient fields may cause severe malfunction in equipment even though the average power is low. Therefore, measurement of the waveforms of the electromagnetic disturbances is important when designing digital equipment. To observe such transient radiation fields, the authors have developed a technique for reconstructing an electromagnetic waveform using the complex antenna factor (CAF) (see Ishgami, S. et al., IEE Trans EMC, vol.38 p.424-32, 1996; IEICE Trans. Commun., vol.E-79B, no.4, p.715, 1996). However, CAF is defined only in the presence of plane wave incidence, while the waveforms are usually measured in the vicinity of the radiating source. In order to examine the reconstruction technique using CAF in the near-field measurements, the voltage waveforms exciting a monopole antenna are estimated through reconstructing the magnetic fields and compared with directly measured results.

articleTitle: Microstrip antennas on multilayer cylindrical and quasi-cylindrical structures
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: A method to analyze cylindrical and quasi-cylindrical multilayer microstrip antennas is presented. The method is based on the integral equation technique in combination with spectral domain approach. In the first step the dyadic Green's function of the cylindrical structure is derived in the spectral domain by the use of an equivalent circuit. By introducing a perturbation term an approximate solution for the quasi-cylindrical structure is found. Numerical results for the cylindrical and quasi-cylindrical structures are shown.

articleTitle: On the convergence of simple FDTD feed models for antennas
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: We examine the convergence of FDTD calculations of the input admittance of a simple dipole antenna for two different feed models. These results show that as the size of the cell is reduced, one must be careful to properly position and scale the elements in the feed model (such as the contours along which voltage and current are determined) to obtain convergence for the impedance.

articleTitle: Analysis of a corrugated horn using the BOR-FDTD method
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: The BOR-FDTD technique is used to determine the return loss and radiation patterns of a corrugated horn. The perfectly matched layer (PML) absorbing boundary conditions are used for the computation. The source excitation is a sine-modulated Gaussian pulse, spatially weighted with the cylindrical TE/sub 11/ mode fields. The results for the return loss and radiation patterns are compared with those obtained using a commercial package based on the mode matching/method of moments technique. The results show excellent agreement.

articleTitle: Modeling shadow region due to propagation through discrete random media
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: Because of the development of cellular systems, the prediction of the propagation through discrete random media appears to be very useful. Recent works have shown the existence of a region with additional attenuation to that caused by free-space propagation. This paper aims at approaching the main phenomena responsible for this attenuation with an analytic formulation. The results are essentially based on the resolution of the problem of diffraction by thin-wire structures with the method of moments (MoM).

articleTitle: High-order method of moment method with point-based discretization
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: A high-order method of moment (HO-MoM) that is as efficient as a Nystrom solution method is introduced. In this scheme, both the testing and the basis functions are expanded into a set of smooth basis distributed over the scattering surface. However, through a simple transformation, the outer integration is eliminated resulting in a point-based form of the integral equation. Specifically, the integral equation is simply sampled at discrete quadrature abscissa points. It is demonstrated that this technique provides true high-order convergence for the current and RCS of canonical geometries.

articleTitle: Using electromagnetic field calculations to understand the complexity of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) at high magnetic field strength
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: Electromagnetic field calculations have often been utilized, even for fundamental problems, in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). For such calculations to be truly useful, however, they must fulfill two criteria. First, they must be accurate descriptions of the problem. For MRI this can be difficult due to complex electrical behavior of RF coils and the presence of the human subject. Second, the results must be expressed in a form that has some meaning in the MR experiment. Drawing from several sets of calculation and experiments that we have performed, we describe the methods that we use to perform calculations and relate results to the MR experiment. We show that even very complicated signal intensity patterns seen in experimental images at 300 MHz in a head-sized phantom can be explained with Maxwell's equations and current MR theory when the theory of reciprocity is applied correctly. The methods and results presented demonstrate, unequivocally, that flip angle and coil sensitivity are related to circularly-polarized components of the B1 field with opposite polarization. We have also demonstrated the importance of considering the experimental methods used in defining the RF excitation pulse in order to relate results to experiment accurately.

articleTitle: Analysis of arrays of printed antennas with a 2D multiresolution method of moment
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: The method of moments is a well known and largely used electromagnetic analysis technique. This technique often becomes computationally intractable when fine discretisations or (and) large structures are involved. In both cases, the technique leads to store a large and dense matrix and the calculation time as well as the memory storage increase dramatically. To overcome these difficulties, the use of wavelet bases has been proposed. In this paper, Chui-Haar (see Numerical Methods of Approximation Theory, vol.9. p.53-75) wavelets are used as basis and testing functions in the MoM (MRMoM). The application of the multiresolution analysis (MRA) permits one to obtain sparse linear systems and then to improve the performances of the MoM. This paper presents the application of the MRMoM for modelling of arrays of microstrip antennas. The formulation of the MRMoM for planar antennas is presented. The aim of this paper is to presents new numerical results which demonstrate the MRMoM capabilities. A linear array of electromagnetically coupled (EMC) dipoles is first proposed. Secondly, a 16 elements planar array of rectangular microstrip patches is analysed.

articleTitle: Bi-mode time-space multiplexing antenna array for multi-targets detection in automotive application
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: A novel antenna array scheme BTSM is proposed where time-space multiplexing technology is used and advantages of panorama and detail modes are combined. Compared with conventional MAA, this array has high capability for multi-target detection, smaller size, lower cost and smaller computation. BTSM FMCW radar systems will allow lane prediction and the classification of objects, thus making possible the intelligent interpretation of traffic scenes.

articleTitle: Contribution of the triple effects to the monostatic RCS of arbitrary targets modeled by plane facets
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: A method to evaluate the contribution of the triple reflection and the iteration between an edge and two facets to the monostatic RCS of arbitrary bodies is presented. The approach is based on a combination of physical optics (PO) and geometrical optics (GO) for the triple reflection and on the equivalent current method (ECM) and geometrical optics (GO) for the iteration edge-facets. The bodies are modeled by plane facets composed by dielectric and magnetic material including losses.

articleTitle: Resonant frequency of dipole antennas with crank sections in dual-band arrays
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: This paper presents the relation between the resonant frequency and the length of the dipole, which is an important parameter in antenna design. This relation is derived from a comparison between the inductance of the dipole and of a half wavelength dipole having the same resonant frequency. In addition, the theory is confirmed by numerical results.

articleTitle: Wideband U-slot microstrip antenna using CPW feed
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: The coplanar waveguide (CPW) has been researched due to several attractive features in comparison with the microstrip line. The attractions are wide bandwidth, better impedance matching, easy integration of solid state active devices and low radiation loss (see Nesic, A., 1983; Menzel, W. and Grabherr, 1991). Especially, in microwave and millimeter wave applications, slot coupling fed by CPW has several useful properties. A U-slot microstrip antenna using a CPW feed is proposed. The proposed antenna has wide bandwidth and can decrease the number of substrates, compared with an antenna using a conventional slot-coupled microstrip feed line. Antenna designs and detail of experimental results are described and discussed.

articleTitle: Time-domain analysis in non-harmonious net of an antenna with two parallel elements using potential function's approximation
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: A transient analysis of an antenna, generally, can be made in two ways. The first one is based on analysis in frequency domain, and the second one is based on time domain analysis. The analysis of an antenna with two parallel identical elements, in this paper, is based on time-domain analysis. The antenna is fed with an ideal voltage generator. A method for determination of the current distribution along the elements is developed first. For this purpose, the potential functions values are obtained, using the method of characteristics. The current distribution is determined with the current values in previous times and computed values of the potential functions. For illustration of the exactness of the presented method, the results obtained for the input admittance of an antenna are compared with results computed with another method. The method presented for analysis of an antenna with two elements in a non-harmonious net, performs a continuation in developing the basic method for analysis of a symmetrical cylindrical antenna in a harmonious net. This gives the opportunity of the method's use in more general cases.

articleTitle: Fast computation of multi-layered Green's function
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: The GPOF method, along with an interpolation routine, is used to calculate the complex image of the Green's function with reduced computational effort. This method takes advantage of the smoothly varying nature of the complex images of the Green's function in multi-layered media to accelerate the computation of the Green's function.

articleTitle: A novel multitarget adaptive array algorithm for wireless CDMA systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: In CDMA systems several users occupy the same frequency band. An adaptive array utilized in such an environment must be able to separate and extract each user's signal simultaneously. Thus in order to avoid bandwidth overhead, it is preferred that the algorithm used to adapt the weights work without a training sequence, i.e., the algorithm should be blind. LS-DRMTA is such a kind algorithm. We propose a modification in LS-DRMTA in a way that the weight generated by the new algorithm multipath least squares despread respread multitarget array (MLS-DRMTA) can produce a radiation pattern with beams directed toward the several desired signal multipaths.

articleTitle: Transient response of a thin wire buried in a real ground
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: The transient behaviour of a thin wire buried in the earth and excited by an incident field is analyzed. The problem is formulated directly in the time domain via the space-time Hallen integral equation. The Hallen integral equation is solved by the time domain Galerkin-Bubnov boundary element procedure and the transient response of the buried wire illuminated by the electromagnetic pulse (EMP) is obtained.

articleTitle: Statistical characteristics of Alfven and hydromagnetic gradient waves in a randomly inhomogeneous plasma
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: Features of low-frequency waves phenomena in homogeneous magnetized plasma have been well studied. However, the influence of inhomogeneity and nonstationarity of plasma parameters on statistical characteristics of hydrodynamic waves has not been investigated in detail. Little attention is devoted to magnetohydrodynamic waves in turbulent plasma streams, observed both in cosmic and laboratory conditions. The article studies the hydrodynamic wave propagation statistical characteristics in a cold plasma in the presence of external magnetic field.

articleTitle: A novel, highly effective preconditioner for solving the finite element-boundary integral matrix equation of 3-D scattering
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: We present an efficient finite element-boundary integral (FE-BI) solution. Instead of replacing the FE-BI system with the FE-ABC system and improving the solution through iteration, we use the finite element-absorbing boundary condition (FE-ABC) matrix as a preconditioner and then seek the solution using a Krylov subspace based method. Both mathematical analysis and numerical results are presented to show the high effectiveness of the preconditioner and the fast convergence of the iterative solution.

articleTitle: Multipath scattering model for LMDS
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: A model for multipath interference that more accurately depicts scattering mechanisms at frequencies allotted for local multipoint distribution service (LMDS) is proposed. The LMDS system addressed in this paper uses orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM). The proposed model is not statistical as is normally the case in most LMDS studies but relies on the geometrical theory of diffraction (G'I'D) that uses ray tracing techniques to model multipath scattering behavior in the low-to-mid GHz frequency range. Our study shows that the GTD multipath scattering model provides significant insight into the performance of LMDS systems operating in the GHz range. It is shown that OFDM performance may degrade significantly depending on the number and geometric features of the sources of multipath scattering. This work provides some insight into where it is appropriate to house or locate LMDS systems.

articleTitle: Analysis of quarter-wave shorted patch antenna
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: A special domain method is used to analyze a quarter-wave shorted rectangular patch antenna driven by a coaxial probe. Using the entire domain distribution function for the patch current, the self-impedance of the patch and the mutual coupling between the patch and probe are calculated using the free space Green's function. The singularity in the kernel of the integral equation is avoided by selecting different integration schemes for source and field integrations. The input impedance and radiation pattern of the quarter-wave shorted rectangular patch are computed and validated against measurements.

articleTitle: Inductive magnetic currents and radiation characteristics of planar and linear arrays: analysis of resembling behaviours
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: In this paper, the method of moments is employed to analyze planar and linear finite phased arrays of radiating slots fed by rectangular waveguides and open-end rectangular waveguides. The equivalent magnetic currents and active patterns due to these elements in phased arrays are discussed in detail. The relationship between linear and planar arrays was also analyzed.

articleTitle: Measurement system for the Green Bank Telescope
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: The Green Bank Telescope (GBT) at the National Radio Astronomy Observatory (NRAO) site in Green Bank, WV, was completed in June 2000. At the time of writing, the GBT is undergoing testing of the various systems and characterization of the actual structural modes. It is the largest, fully-steerable radio telescope in the world. The main reflector which is a solid-surface paraboloid has an unblocked 100-meter projected aperture. The telescope will operate at prime focus from 25 MHz to 1200 MHz and at Gregorian focus from 1.15 GHz to /spl ges/ 100 GHz. It is a state-of-the-art instrument with an active surface to compensate for deformations of the primary reflector backup structure due to external loads. The GBT has a unique six-degree of freedom subreflector and a three-degree of freedom prime focus mount that allow realigning of the optics which is required as the telescope moves in elevation. A receiver turret that holds 8 secondary focus receivers will provide rapid frequency agility for the telescope. This paper describes the metrology system, based on laser rangefinders, that has been developed at NRAO for the realization of the active surface and precision pointing of the GBT.

articleTitle: A double folded, capacitive-fed, cavity-backed microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: A novel folded capacitive-fed microstrip antenna with length of /spl lambda//3 and placed over a cavity backing is proposed. Compared to the small rectangular patch antenna by Luk (see Electronics Letters, vol.34, no.25, p.2366-67, 1998 ), our proposed antenna has a large impedance bandwidth of 20.1%. The cross-polarization level is /spl sim/-17dB.

articleTitle: Novel approach to construct temporal basis functions for time-domain integral equation method
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: Time-domain integral equation (TDIE) methods, for the solution of transient electromagnetic problems have steadily increased in popularity. A novel construction method is presented to design the new temporal basis function. We first specify the principal properties of the desirable temporal basis function. According to these properties and choosing a suitable function with some parameters, we construct a nonlinear programming problem with respect to these parameters, from which the new temporal basis function can be derived. The obtained temporal function has the any-order continuous derivative and is not a truncated version of any function. By using the construction method, a new temporal function, namely, the rational fractional temporal function, is also presented. The numerical result shows that the new temporal function pushes the occurrence of the late-time instability of the transient simulation further down in time when compared to the previous temporal functions.

articleTitle: Analysis of ferrite-loaded cavity-backed antennas including nonlinear and nonuniform magnetization effects
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: In this paper, for the first time according to the authors' knowledge, the formal nonlinear magnetostatic analysis is used to compute the spatial nonuniform permeability tensor of the ferrite samples in antenna applications. The 3-D nonlinear magnetostatic problem is first solved with the aid of a nodal FEM solution, and then the hybrid finite element method/method of moments (FEM/MoM) full-wave analysis is used to compute various antenna/scattering characteristics of the cavity backed antenna.

articleTitle: The development of electromagnetic pulse well logging system and its experiment studies
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: The paper present the experiment studies with our developed laboratory transient electromagnetic pulse logging system. The system, assembled as a tool, consists of several subsystems mainly such as the transient pulse signal generator, the transmitting/receiving antennas with resistive loadings, the time-domain sampling unit, the computer interfaces and the software packages for system control and data processing. By using the tool in the simulation well, four modeling formations are investigated in the experiments to verify the performance of the EMP logging method. From the results in the paper, it is realized that the methods used to process measured data and analyze responses are vital to distinguish the modeling underground formations. The time-domain holographic responses (TDHR) is obtained by the measurements with our integrated software packages. The main advantage of the TDHR is that the general image of the measured objects can be intuitively exhibited. To further inspect the information of the formation figures, the main pulse responses (MPR) and the time-scanning responses (TSR) are also proposed and employed in the paper. It is shown that the analysis method of the TSR is more promising and effective for the identification of objects.

articleTitle: Wideband subarray systems: evolution of a research area
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: R.W.P. King has always insisted that his students look beyond the trivial to uncover the subtleties that, (more often than not) require detailed electromagnetic analysis and reveal fundamental properties. The purpose of this paper is to look at an important topic in scanning arrays to show how the interaction of obvious geometrical features and very subtle electromagnetic features are shaping this evolving technology. This paper discusses developments in the technology of transform-fed wideband scanning arrays. These antennas were introduced over 40 years ago, and proposed for a large number of scanning applications, but because of poor efficiency and high cost, have not found application in fielded systems. However, technological innovations including MEMS phase shifters and digital beamforming have re-focused attention on these systems, which for many applications remain the most viable array architecture for large wide band arrays.

articleTitle: A design procedure for classical offset inverse Cassegrain antennas with circular apertures
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: The classical offset inverse Cassegrain configuration is proposed as a reflector antenna geometry. Its sub and main reflectors are concave ellipsoid and convex paraboloid, respectively. This geometry is potentially capable of yielding a wide field of view while being efficiently illuminated by small feeds. An efficient design procedure was derived for them, and verified with two examples. The starting design parameters of the procedure are convenient since they can be easily related to basic system constraints. The scattering characteristics of the two examples validate the design procedure by indicating that all optimum geometry has been obtained.

articleTitle: FDTD simulation of the angular correlation function of objects buried in continuous random media
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: Natural media are often inhomogeneous and cannot be described in a deterministic manner, so a statistical model should be employed instead. In analytical studies, statistical models often describe a medium as an effective or mean permittivity (or permeability) with random fluctuations that follow a prescribed correlation function. A single realization (assuming spatial ergodicity) or ensemble of random media with correlation functions chosen to describe the medium of interest are used to study the statistical properties of the scattered and transmitted fields. In this paper, a 3-D finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) scheme is used to model the scattering from an object in a continuous random medium. FDTD techniques have been previously applied to scattering from random rough surfaces and randomly placed objects in a homogeneous background, but little has been done to simulate continuous random media with embedded objects where volume-scattering effects are important. The random medium parameters in this case are approximately based on particular soil models, with subsurface sensing applications in mind. Soil naturally contains fluctuations in density, material, and moisture, which may effect the scattering results. The scattered field from the random medium, with and without an object present, is studied using the angular correlation function (ACF).

articleTitle: A hierarchical time-domain modulation scheme for wideband communications in a dispersive multipath channel
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: In this paper a time-domain modulation scheme for ultra-wideband communications is proposed and the performance of such modulation scheme in a highly dispersive channel is evaluated using a coherent and physics-based propagation model. In this scheme a relatively large number of orthogonal waveforms, that are scalable in time and frequency domains (like wavelets), are modulated (pulse position or amplitude modulation) with a piece of information data individually and transmitted through the channel. This scheme offers two major advantages: (1) noting that pathloss and channel characteristics are very much frequency dependent, at least a portion of information reaches distant observation points, (2) each waveform can easily be radiated from a small and relatively narrowband antenna and hence issues related to the design of efficient, dispersionless ultra-wideband antennas is circumvented. This approach also allows for data categorization according to a specific hierarchy. To demonstrate the advantages mentioned and assess the performance of such system, an ultra-wideband wave propagation in a forested environment over a frequency range of 10-210 MHz, is presented.

articleTitle: Planar dielectric image line antenna arrays using Y-junctions
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: Dielectric image line (DIL), a rectangular dielectric cylinder on a ground plane, is an open low-loss transmission line for millimeter-wave frequencies. By introducing periodic gratings, linear leaky wave antenna arrays have been made from DIL. A DIL power divider can be constructed by widening the width of its input line and then splitting the dielectric into two output arms. Two planar arrays fed by dielectric image line Y-junctions are described. Planar arrays are used to reduce the radiation patterns' beamwidth in two orthogonal planes. Beam scanning, using an electro-mechanical actuator, is demonstrated for one of the planar antennas.

articleTitle: A Dirac-like inference of Maxwell's equations
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: The purpose of this article is to present an elementary derivation of Maxwell's equations suitable for an opening lecture in a modern applied electromagnetism course. It is inspired by Dirac and the way he inferred his celebrated equation. Interestingly enough, his arguments, which are gradually fading away from modern quantum field theory courses, regain their vitality in the context of classical electrodynamics. Consequently, this derivation starts with (1) the wave equation and leans on (2) the Huygens principle and (3) transversal polarization of light as an electromagnetic wave. All three ingredients are firmly rooted among the experimental facts.

articleTitle: Ionospheric total electron content measurements by analyzing GPS data of Ankara, Turkey
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
abstract: In this paper, we present results from analysis of GPS signals received in Ankara, Turkey. The main purpose of this study is to introduce a new technique, which uses pseudorange differences instead of phase differences, that enables us to make rough estimates of the TEC by using GPS observables. In this algorithm, we use the time difference between pseudoranges of L1 and L2 signals to obtain hourly TEC value. The results for the coverage area of the system is presented.

articleTitle: Staircase approximation for transients of multisection dispersive transmission lines with nonlinear loads
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium. 2001 Digest. Held in conjunction with: USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting (Cat. No.01CH37229)
